# Minimum Element After Replacement With Digit Sum.

@example The digit sums are 5 + 7 = 12, 4 + 0 + 3 = 7 and 8 + 8 = 16.
[57,403,88]
=> 7

@example 2000 is the largest number, but its digit sum, 2, is the smallest; 6 and 15 both have digit sum 6.
[6,2000,15]
=> 2

@example All three digit sums are 11.
[38,47,56]
=> 11

# 10000, the only number with five digits, has digit sum 1.
[10000]
=> 1

# 9999 has the largest possible digit sum, 36.
[9999,9999,9999]
=> 36

# The smallest digit sum comes first.
[100,99,58]
=> 1

# The smallest digit sum comes last.
[4321,789,5000]
=> 5

# The smallest number does not have the smallest digit sum.
[8,2010]
=> 3

# The answer is a digit sum, not the number it belongs to.
[45,72]
=> 9

# All the numbers are the same.
[1234,1234,1234,1234]
=> 10

# A single digit is its own digit sum.
[7,3,9,5]
=> 3

# Powers of ten all have digit sum 1.
[10,100,1000,10000,1]
=> 1

# Every digit sum is large.
[9998,8999,9899]
=> 35

[9990,9909,9099]
=> 27

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[8874,9260,899,683,4858,9526,106]
=> 7

@gen 2 small
[1129,9484,9618,4398,3258]
=> 13

@gen 3 small
[4527,1524,121,443,9804,9531,9865,544]
=> 4

@gen 4 small
[620,541,52,158]
=> 7

@gen 5 small
[5643,739,34,7135,5635,12]
=> 3

@gen 6 small
[881,9527]
=> 17
